newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa higher in lackluster midday trade.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa higher in lackluster midday trade.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures hovered at moderately higher levels in dull trading at midsession, bolstered by local shortcovering, dealers said.
"It's absolutely dead," said one trader. "Nothing is going on. We've been trading for between $1,525 and $1,530 (a tonne basis September) for the last two hours."
At 1207 EDT, benchmark September was up $13 at $1,526 a tonne, traded $1,537 to $1,515. Second-month December was $11 higher at $1,571, while the back months gained $3 to $13.
Cocoa prices headed higher at the outset, defying pre-opening expectations, on light speculative buying, traders said.
A bout of shortcovering by locals lifted the September contract to the highs, but scale-up trade selling trimmed gains and prevented a test of chart resistance at $1,540.

On the charts, traders said that after the $1,540 level, September would find resistance at $1,547-$1,550, followed by a gap between $1,561 and $1,570. On the downside, support was seen at $1,513-$1,510.
Turnover as of 1100 was thin at an estimated 2,367 lots.
